title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing, fairness, starvation prevention, timeouts
author: Ethan Park
description: Context: The continuous-batcher scheduler has been observed to favor high-throughput request shapes at the expense of low-volume, latency-sensitive callers resulting in starvation and occasional unbounded queue growth during uneven traffic patterns. Motivation: Improve fairness and starvation prevention without regressing throughput or increasing p95 tail latency. Summary of changes: 1) Introduce a hybrid queueing policy that combines weighted round-robin across caller buckets with dynamic priority boosts for long-waiting requests; 2) Add per-bucket starvation window tracking and a configurable starvation_score that forces priority elevation when a bucket exceeds the window; 3) Implement soft timeouts at the scheduler level that convert long-queued requests into lower-cost fallback routes instead of outright failures; 4) Emit new observability metrics (scheduler.queue_ms, scheduler.queue_length_by_bucket, scheduler.starvation_count, scheduler.timeout_elevations) and tracing spans for queueing operations; 5) Add backpressure signal propagation to upstream RPC layer so clients can route to fallback model variants earlier under sustained saturation; 6) Minor KV-cache instrumentation to surface hit/miss correlation with batching behavior for future tuning. Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed by runtime team and SRE (ENG-7890) - [x] Unit tests for queueing policy and starvation detection - [x] Integration perf tests against synthetic traffic (spiky/uniform/zipf) - [x] Canary rollout gating via feature flag - [x] Observability dashboards and alerts added Motivation and tradeoffs: The hybrid policy keeps throughput by preferring larger batches while the starvation_score ensures latency-sensitive callers are served within bounded time. Soft timeouts trade a small number of graceful fallbacks for system-wide stability under pathological loads. Testing and results: Microbenchmarks: no-regression in peak throughput (<3% variance) and median latency within noise. Tail improvements: 95th latency improved by ~18% for low-volume buckets under mixed traffic (zipf with hot 10% tenants). Starvation prevention: starvation_count dropped to zero in synthetic runs where previous scheduler hit >200 events/hour. CI: full test suite and perf harness passed after a retry of flaky e2e that was unrelated to scheduling. Rollout plan: gated canary for 2% of traffic for 24h, monitor scheduler.* metrics and p95/p99 release windows, expand to 25% then full roll after 48h if no alerts. Related work: follows up on prior continuous-batcher tuning PRs and reuses the metrics conventions introduced in previous perf patches. Docs: added a short note in docs/continuous-batcher.md on new config knobs. Breaking changes: none. Notes for reviewers: pay attention to starvation window defaults and whether the soft timeout policy should be opt-in per deployment. Implementation details are small and contained to continuous_batcher/scheduler.py, continuous_batcher/policy.py, runtime/kv_cache_instrumentation.py, infra/observability/metrics_registry.py, tests/perf/test_batcher_fairness.py, tests/unit/test_starvation_detection.py, and docs/continuous-batcher.md.
